review_note:
# Independent primitive-register verifier review

Reviewed the exact source hashes in independent-register-review.json against maintained term_patterns.py, pattern_codec.py and term_circuits.py. No unresolved semantic defect found. This is a read-only source/math review; no suites, table compilation or Lean builds were repeated.

The helper scratch discipline is consistent at actual call sites. ReadNode touches only the original18 helper registers; the full cursor, current parameters/formula, proof scan state and gate saves live in distinct globals. Proof lookup scans exactly premise+1 previous rows. Gates save cursor and path bit before node reads, preserve both paths, and implement the maintained positive-equal-prefix/terminal-mismatch relation. The full structural pass validates unused nodes and rows and requires an empty suffix, so selected-prefix ReadNode cannot bypass malformed unused data. References and proof-premise ordering are checked before semantics. Truth, MP orientation and virtual-zero alias, GEN, all fixed trusted patterns, both bundle gates and every copy of fixed falsity match the maintained verifier.

One concrete compiler-entry obligation was found: read_node labels its helper root main().0 and search later gives that name to the full root; Wade reachable selects the first named match. Direct-int structured tests are unaffected. Parent acknowledged the issue and will erase all sequence names and assign only the actual search root before table reachability/naming/generation. This is required for a valid whole-program cost; it is not a reported logical verifier bug.

Natural increments enumerate each finite binary word exactly once through word_code/code_word; the within-length order differs from the maintained length-lex iterator but fairness and proof existence are unchanged. All56 declared registers, their selectors, verifier, enumeration/reset, dispatcher and initializer must be charged for a full binary table. No new state-bound or compiler/blank-run theorem follows from the finite fast-interpreter checks. Only explicit local arithmetic helpers are contracted; parsing and reference proof checking are not delegated to the Python verifier.
